test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is an autobiography of a Bengali illiterate woman who secretly acquired literacy skills to read sacred texts in an age when girls and women were denied education and deemed fit only for household chores?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Amar Jiban by Rassundari Devi**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **"Aamar Jiban," **published in **1876**, stands as the title of **Rassundari Devi's autobiography**, marking a significant milestone as the first autobiography composed by an Indian woman and also the earliest one penned by any** Bengali female**.
 
• Through this work, Devi provides insights into the status of women within **19th-century Indian society**, shedding light on the prevalent inequality and hardships they endured.
 
• Notably, "Aamar Jiban" holds the distinction of being the first full-length autobiography published in the Bengali language.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **"Ente Katha"** (My Story) is an autobiography penned by Kamala Surayya, also known as Madhavikutty, in the year 1973. Surayya was driven to write this account when she fell ill and feared she might not survive.
 
• **"Jina Amucha,"** authored by Baby Kamble, is a compelling and poignant autobiographical piece written in Marathi. The English translation of "Jina Amucha" is titled "The Prisons We Broke."
